title: अध्याय १३

items.speaker: ; पुत्र उवाच
items.text:
अहं वैश्यकुले जातो जन्मन्यस्मात्तु सप्तमे ।
समतीते गवां रोधं निपाने कृतवान् पुरा ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
ahaṃ vaiśyakule jāto janmanyasmāttu saptame |
samatīte gavāṃ rodhaṃ nipāne kṛtavān purā || 1 ||

items.text:
पात्यमानस्य मे तत्र साग्रं वर्षशतं गतम् ।
महातापार्तितप्तस्य तृष्णादाहान्वितस्य च ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
pātyamānasya me tatra sāgraṃ varṣaśataṃ gatam |
mahātāpārtitaptasya tṛṣṇādāhānvitasya ca || 4 ||

items.text:
तत्राह्लादकरः सद्यः पवनः सुखशीतलः ।
करम्भ-बालुकाकुम्भ-मध्यस्थो मे समागतः ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
tatrāhlādakaraḥ sadyaḥ pavanaḥ sukhaśītalaḥ |
karambha-bālukākumbha-madhyastho me samāgataḥ || 5 ||

items.text:
तत्सम्पर्कादशेषाणां नाभवद्यातना नृणाम् ।
मम चापि यथा स्वर्गे स्वर्गिणां निर्वृतिः परा ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
tatsamparkādaśeṣāṇāṃ nābhavadyātanā nṛṇām |
mama cāpi yathā svarge svargiṇāṃ nirvṛtiḥ parā || 6 ||

items.text:
याम्यश्च पुरुषो घोरो दण्डहस्तोऽशनिप्रभः ।
पुरतो दर्शयन् मार्गमिति एहीति वगथ ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
yāmyaśca puruṣo ghoro daṇḍahasto'śaniprabhaḥ |
purato darśayan mārgamiti ehīti vagatha || 8 ||

items.text:
पुरुषः स तदा दृष्ट्वा यातनाशतसंकुलम् ।
नरकं प्राह तं याम्यं किङ्करं कृपयान्वितः ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
puruṣaḥ sa tadā dṛṣṭvā yātanāśatasaṃkulam |
narakaṃ prāha taṃ yāmyaṃ kiṅkaraṃ kṛpayānvitaḥ || 9 ||

items.speaker: ; पुरुष उवाच
items.text:
भो याम्यपुरुषाचक्ष्व किं मया दुष्कृतं कृतम् ।
येनेदं यातनाभीम् प्राप्तोऽस्मि नरकं परम् ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
bho yāmyapuruṣācakṣva kiṃ mayā duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam |
yenedaṃ yātanābhīm prāpto'smi narakaṃ param || 10 ||

items.text:
विपश्चिदिति विख्यातो जनकानामहं कुले ।
जातो विदेहविषये सम्यङ्मनुजपालकः ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
vipaściditi vikhyāto janakānāmahaṃ kule |
jāto videhaviṣaye samyaṅmanujapālakaḥ || 11 ||

items.text:
यज्ञैर्मयेष्टं बहुभिर्धर्मतः पालिता मही ।
नोत्सृष्टश्चैव संग्रामो नातिथिर्विमुखो गतः ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
yajñairmayeṣṭaṃ bahubhirdharmataḥ pālitā mahī |
notsṛṣṭaścaiva saṃgrāmo nātithirvimukho gataḥ || 12 ||

items.text:
पितृ-देवर्षि-भृत्याश्च न चापचरिता मया ।
कृता स्पृहा च न मया परस्त्रीविभवादिषु ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
pitṛ-devarṣi-bhṛtyāśca na cāpacaritā mayā |
kṛtā spṛhā ca na mayā parastrīvibhavādiṣu || 13 ||

items.text:
पर्वकालेषु पितरस्तिथिकालेषु देवताः ।
पुरुषं स्वयमायान्ति निपानमिव धेनवः ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
parvakāleṣu pitarastithikāleṣu devatāḥ |
puruṣaṃ svayamāyānti nipānamiva dhenavaḥ || 14 ||

items.text:
यतस्ते विमुखा यान्ति निश्वस्य गृहमेधिनः ।
तस्मादिष्टश्च पूर्तश्च धमौ द्वावपि नश्यतः ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
yataste vimukhā yānti niśvasya gṛhamedhinaḥ |
tasmādiṣṭaśca pūrtaśca dhamau dvāvapi naśyataḥ || 15 ||

items.text:
पितृनिश्वासविध्वस्तं सप्तजन्मार्जितं शुभम् ।
त्रिजन्मप्रभवं दैवो निश्वासो हन्त्यसंशयम् ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
pitṛniśvāsavidhvastaṃ saptajanmārjitaṃ śubham |
trijanmaprabhavaṃ daivo niśvāso hantyasaṃśayam || 16 ||

items.text:
तस्माद् दैवे च पित्र्ये च नित्यमेवोद्यतोऽभवम् ।
सोऽहं कथमिमं प्राप्तो नरङ्क भृशदारुणम् ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
tasmād daive ca pitrye ca nityamevodyato'bhavam |
so'haṃ kathamimaṃ prāpto naraṅka bhṛśadāruṇam || 17 ||

en_summary: The son tells his father of his own experience in hell. In his seventh birth before this one he was born in a vaishya (merchant) family and once kept cows away from a drinking place. For that deed he fell into a terrible hell full of flames and iron-beaked birds, with mud made of the blood of bodies crushed in machines, and loud with the cries of sinners being cut. He spent over a hundred years there, burning and thirsty. Then suddenly a cool, pleasant wind reached him in the midst of the hot sand-pots, and from its touch all the beings there were freed from torment, and he felt the joy that people in heaven feel. Looking up in wonder, they saw nearby a most excellent man, with a terrible servant of Yama, staff in hand and shining like lightning, walking ahead and saying 'Come this way.' Seeing the hell full of hundreds of tortures, the man, full of pity, asked Yama's servant what sin he had committed to be brought to this hell. He was Vipashchit, born in the family of the Janakas in Videha; he had ruled well, performed many sacrifices, protected the earth by dharma, never fled from battle, never turned a guest away, never wronged ancestors, gods, sages or servants, and never desired other men's wives or wealth. Ancestors come to a man on the days of the moon's changes and gods on the lunar days, like cows to a drinking place; if they go away sighing, the householder's merit from sacrifices and good works is lost (the sigh of the ancestors destroys the merit of seven births, that of the gods the merit of three). So he had always been diligent in rites for gods and ancestors; how then had he come to this terrible hell?
